title: A. Another Popcount Problem
statement:
You are given two integers $$n$$ and $$k$$.

Your task is to construct a sequence $$a$$ consisting of $$k$$ non-negative integers $$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_k$$ such that:

You only need to output the maximum possible value of $$\sum_{i=1}^{k} \operatorname{popcount}(a_i)$$.

Here, $$\operatorname{popcount}(x)$$ denotes the number of $$1$$ bits in the binary representation of $$x$$. For example, $$\operatorname{popcount}(6) = \operatorname{popcount}((110)_2) = 2$$, and $$\operatorname{popcount}(0) = 0$$.

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$t$$ ($$1 $\leq t \leq 10^3$$$). The description of the test cases follows.

Each of the next $$t$$ lines contains two integers $$n$$ and $$k$$ ($$1 $\leq n, k \leq 10^6$$$) — the maximum allowed sum of the sequence and the length of the sequence, respectively.

For each test case, output a single integer — the maximum possible value of $$\sum_{i=1}^{k} \operatorname{popcount}(a_i)$$.

In the first test case, $$n=2$$ and $$k=1$$. We can choose $$a = [1]$$ or $$a = [2]$$. In both cases, the sum of popcounts is $$1$$.

In the second test case, $$n=3$$ and $$k=1$$. We can choose $$a = [3]$$, since $$(3)_2 = (11)_2$$, $$\operatorname{popcount}(3) = 2$$.

In the third test case, $$n=6$$ and $$k=2$$. We can choose $$a = [3, 3]$$. The sum is $$3 + 3 = 6 $\leq 6$$$, and the total popcount is $$\operatorname{popcount}(3) + \operatorname{popcount}(3) = 2 + 2 = 4$$.
input: Input Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$t$$ ($$1 $\leq t \leq 10^3$$$). The description of the test cases follows. Each of the next $$t$$ lines contains two integers $$n$$ and $$k$$ ($$1 $\leq n, k \leq 10^6$$$) — the maximum allowed sum of the sequence and the length of the sequence, respectively.
output: Output For each test case, output a single integer — the maximum possible value of $$\sum_{i=1}^{k} \operatorname{popcount}(a_i)$$.
